headline: High: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces can amplify prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when paired with Khoj’s broad filesystem-backed retrieval.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces, so content from one can plausibly reach the other through shared workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation between retrieved content and tool instructions. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so uncertainty keeps it below high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is ingested into Khoj retrieval without provenance labels, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or webhook workflow passes untrusted text into either agent’s instruction channel, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted OpenMetadata text into Khoj.
Add provenance tags to retrieved snippets before they reach prompts.
Require explicit human review for any instruction-like content.
Restrict OpenMetadata webhooks/MCP to allowlisted schemas.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the integration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge metadata through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If the pair shares data, sensitive notes can be exposed to a broader metadata plane and then emitted through OpenMetadata integrations. The default surface breadth makes leakage materially plausible.
conditions: IF personal notes or indexed documents are synchronized into OpenMetadata metadata objects, leakage risk is present.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs forward those objects to third parties, exfiltration expands.
mitigations: Limit synced fields to non-sensitive metadata only.
Turn off webhook forwarding for note-derived records.
Separate credentials for Khoj and OpenMetadata.
Review and redact sensitive documents before indexing.
requires-engineering: implement field-level access controls and DLP filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read_filesystem and broad network egress, while OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Even without write access from Khoj, both can mutate shared external resources through APIs or metadata workflows, creating overlapping authority and race conditions. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so conflict is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same metadata or document source, concurrent updates can conflict.
IF OpenMetadata workflows trigger on Khoj-derived changes, stale writes or duplicate actions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces or projects per agent.
Pause one agent during bulk syncs.
Use optimistic concurrency checks on shared records.
Review API write permissions for both agents.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional update coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieval-grounded answers from personal notes, and OpenMetadata is built around data collaboration and governance workflows that can consume upstream outputs. If OpenMetadata treats Khoj’s output as authoritative, a mistaken retrieval can cascade into incorrect lineage, governance, or operational actions. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the blast radius can extend beyond a single answer.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Khoj-generated summaries without verification, downstream metadata can be corrupted.
IF either agent auto-triggers actions from the other’s text, errors can propagate across workflows.
mitigations: Require human approval before OpenMetadata writes derived facts.
Mark Khoj outputs as untrusted until verified.
Add checksum or source-link validation for imported claims.
Disable auto-action triggers on free-text outputs.
requires-engineering: build verification gates between retrieval and metadata mutation.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while OpenMetadata handles governance and lineage metadata that may include regulated identifiers. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes overlap and the pair can move sensitive metadata across systems, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF personal notes contain regulated data and are synchronized into OpenMetadata, policy review is required.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Inventory regulated fields before syncing.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Disable cross-system export for sensitive records.
Document residency and DPA assumptions.
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware routing and deletion propagation.
